slides.title: The 2026 network review
slides.subtitle: Where the network stands after the Baltic expansion, and what the next year needs
slides.notes: Open with the one number: on-time delivery is back above 94% for the first time since the expansion.

slides.title: The year in four numbers

stats.label: hubs in the network after Riga and Tallinn opened

slides.text: Volume grew faster than cost for the first time in three years. The two new hubs carried the growth; the older hubs absorbed it without new headcount.
slides.callout: Growth is no longer buying reliability at the expense of cost.
slides.notes: Pause on the cost figure — it is the one the board asked about last quarter.

slides.title: What changed in the network
slides.text: Two hubs, one routing model, and a different way of promising delivery dates.

slides.title: Three decisions that moved the numbers
slides.subtitle: Each one was argued over; each one paid back inside the year

bullets.text: Riga and Tallinn opened as full hubs, not cross-docks
sub: Sorting capacity 40k parcels a day each

bullets: Routing moved to the new model in March: one plan per day instead of three
Promised dates are now computed from live capacity, not a fixed table
Peak-season surcharges replaced blanket price rises
Customer service got direct access to the routing plan
slides.callout: The routing model did more for reliability than the new buildings did.
slides.notes: If asked about headcount: Riga 140, Tallinn 95, both within plan.

slides.title: How each hub performed

cards.heading: Warsaw
cards.text: Still the largest node: 38% of volume, on-time 95.1%. Capacity is the constraint from November.

cards.heading: Riga
cards.text: Opened in February, at target volume by June. On-time 93.4% and climbing since the second sorter arrived.

cards.heading: Tallinn
cards.text: Smaller and faster: 91% of parcels sorted within four hours of arrival.

cards.heading: Prague
cards.text: Flat volume, best cost per shipment in the network. The model for the next two openings.

cards.heading: Vienna
cards.text: On-time slipped to 90.8% after the carrier change; recovering since the August renegotiation.

cards.heading: Kraków
cards.text: Handled the Warsaw overflow in peak without a single missed cut-off.

slides.notes: Vienna is the one to watch; the carrier contract runs to March.

slides.title: On-time delivery by quarter
slides.subtitle: Percent of shipments delivered on the promised date
slides.insight: The turn came with the routing model in March, one quarter before the new hubs reached volume. Buildings added capacity; the model added reliability.
slides.callout: Four consecutive quarters of improvement, each from a different lever.
slides.notes: The dip in Q3 2025 was the carrier change in Vienna.

slides.title: Cost per shipment by hub
slides.callout: Every established hub cut cost; the new hubs opened below the network average.
slides.notes: Riga's cost includes the second sorter, which is why it sits above Tallinn.
